title: Plans for concerts and musicians' lost loyalty
summary: Albert hopes to do a few concerts a year, laments disloyal musicians in San Antonio and New Orleans, and says money never mattered to him.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well, I'm hoping that maybe this year I might decide that I've had it. And I might just put this government job down and find myself to try and get maybe one or two concerts a year. And that'll be enough. And tour. Yes, and do a little of that. And this would make the life, the musical career, and my life completed.
Well, one thing that works against you, it seems to me, is that San Antonio doesn't have as many musicians to draw.

Well, you don't have any musicians here. Those that you have at Kentville are so few. They have the groups that they play with. And I'm not about to try to organize a group because it's too hard and it's too taxing. Musicians, they're not loyal anymore in the days when I was playing. Now, if I was in New Orleans, I don't know, I may be wrong in saying this, but maybe I would find about six or seven men that would be interested in organizing a group and staying together. But there again, I noticed in my visits that at one time I see a fellow playing with the group here. Next time I look at him, he's with another group. And here again the next night, he's with another group.
Oh, and everybody's a band leader.

Everybody's a band leader. So that's the thing that I don't know whether my idea would be feasible or not. I doubt that it would be because my ideas of leading a band, I think, are altogether different. The only thing, the only concern with musicians in New Orleans on the whole, I think, now this is a matter of opinion, this is my opinion and nobody else's, that the loyalty isn't there, it's the money that's the big thing. And I have never felt that money was a big thing in my life. Maybe that's why I've thrown away fortunes.
But I would like to have a lot of it now.

Well, I don't want it. I wouldn't do it. I don't believe I'll, I've got, I've got a few nickels. But, I'll put it where it won't worry me. I don't even know it's there. And that's how I want to live. I don't want to live. I want to live, I want to live peaceful. And, I don't want money to change my way of living. And money so often has changed the individual. And that I don't, I want to, like I said, I want to be Don Albert from the time that I came into the world until the time that I leave.
